content:
I talked to @Chris Birkbeck at London Learning Lean about getting differential forms done, and Tau Ceti looks like the way to do it even if it never lands in Mathlib. Floating a roadmap here before I open a PR.

Plan: Ω^k(M; V) = Γ^∞(Alt^k(TM, V)), bundle-valued throughout, up to d²=0, the wedge, and Lie-algebra-valued connection and curvature forms with Bianchi. The connection and curvature layer builds on my own work on connections on principal fibre bundles, with a formal Bianchi-identity layer the roadmap would put on a genuine differential-forms footing. The point of the roadmap is the forms and the operations on them.

@Yury G. Kudryashov: DeRhamCohomology already does a lot of this. It's Apache-licensed but I thought should let you know. Did you hit anything nasty, particularly on the manifold d²=0? And would either of you review the roadmap? You know this material better than anyone in Lean.

And if anyone else here does differential geometry and would review the eventual PR that would be great. I have a draft README + Suggested.lean in the house format and am happy to share.

My eventual aim is a blog post on the gauge theory of the falling cat, which is why I want the connection/curvature-form machinery on a proper differential-forms footing.

Hi Dominic,
I've been working/thinking about this topic for a while. Would you mind reviewing my roadmap here?
https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/178/changes#diff-c366f33e17d0b0777f336f301345f3bd09fc95c752ba86532c14eff4d2a5fb3e

Hi Jack - this is great - I left some comments here: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/178#issuecomment-5467530284 - all positive - if I think of anything else, I will add it later. From what I understood, AIs could populate this quite quickly. I am not sure what you had in mind but I was hoping we could extract useful bits, check them very thoroughly and then add them to Mathlib.
So what happens now? Does it have to be approved somehow? And then AIs somehow can get to work on it?
Yep that's it basically. You may be able to approve it yourself (once any changes you wanted are done) if not let me know and we can have a look.

I don't satisfy the criterion to approve - the only confirmation I wanted was to confirm the general (𝔤-valued / vector-valued) version is what actually gets built, with ℝ the special case, which is what 0.1 says.

Thanks for making me aware of this route to get a Lean version of differential forms and it's great that @Jack McCarthy already had the same idea and produced such a good roadmap.
Ok no problem, I left a review of the roadmap with some changes requested, but once thats done I can approve it.
